newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Endesa rejects World Bank criticism.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Endesa rejects World Bank criticism.

text.p: Chilean power company Endesa rejected criticism from the World Bank that it was not meeting environmental obligations at its Pangue and Ralco projects on the Bio Bio river in southern Chile.
"The Pangue project was conceived in accordance with the most recent trends in management, technology and preservation of the environment," said Endesa's Pangue unit in a statement.

A report in newspaper El Diario, quoting World Bank president James Wolfensohn, said the bank had accused Endesa of dragging its feet on environmental conditions agreed with the Bank's finance unit International Finance Corp (IFC).
The IFC was one of the largest financiers of Pangue, which cost $450 million to build and was completed last year.
Endesa accused ecologists, who have strongly opposed both dams, of being behind the allegations.

"The only conceivable explanation for these observations is the pressure and demands of environmental groups which, using public sensitivity to these issues, look for recognition... to have access to international agencies," it said.
Pangue and Ralco, which both span the cool, forested Bio Bio valley, have been among the most controversial projects in Chile in recent years.
Ralco, which is due to come onstream in 2002, will have a dam seven times larger than Pangue and flood 34 kilometers of the Bio Bio valley.
